Base directory for this skill: /home/node/.claude/skills/agent-browser

# Browser Automation with agent-browser

## Quick start

```bash
agent-browser open <url>        # Navigate to page
agent-browser snapshot -i       # Get interactive elements with refs
agent-browser click @e1         # Click element by ref
agent-browser fill @e2 "text"   # Fill input by ref
agent-browser close             # Close browser
```

## Core workflow

1. Navigate: `agent-browser open <url>`
2. Snapshot: `agent-browser snapshot -i` (returns elements with refs like `@e1`, `@e2`)
3. Interact using refs from the snapshot
4. Re-snapshot after navigation or significant DOM changes

## Commands

### Navigation

```bash
agent-browser open <url>      # Navigate to URL
agent-browser back            # Go back
agent-browser forward         # Go forward
agent-browser reload          # Reload page
agent-browser close           # Close browser
```

### Snapshot (page analysis)

```bash
agent-browser snapshot            # Full accessibility tree
agent-browser snapshot -i         # Interactive elements only (recommended)
agent-browser snapshot -c         # Compact output
agent-browser snapshot -d 3       # Limit depth to 3
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main" # Scope to CSS selector
```

### Interactions (use @refs from snapshot)

```bash
agent-browser click @e1           # Click
agent-browser dblclick @e1        # Double-click
agent-browser fill @e2 "text"     # Clear and type
agent-browser type @e2 "text"     # Type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter         # Press key
agent-browser hover @e1           # Hover
agent-browser check @e1           # Check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e1         # Uncheck checkbox
agent-browser select @e1 "value"  # Select dropdown option
agent-browser scroll down 500     # Scroll page
agent-browser upload @e1 file.pdf # Upload files
```

### Get information

```bash
agent-browser get text @e1        # Get element text
agent-browser get html @e1        # Get innerHTML
agent-browser get value @e1       # Get input value
agent-browser get attr @e1 href   # Get attribute
agent-browser get title           # Get page title
agent-browser get url             # Get current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"   # Count matching elements
```

### Screenshots & PDF

```bash
agent-browser screenshot          # Save to temp directory
agent-browser screenshot path.png # Save to specific path
agent-browser screenshot --full   # Full page
agent-browser pdf output.pdf      # Save as PDF
```

### Wait

```bash
agent-browser wait @e1                     # Wait for element
agent-browser wait 2000                    # Wait milliseconds
agent-browser wait --text "Success"        # Wait for text
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"    # Wait for URL pattern
agent-browser wait --load networkidle      # Wait for network idle
```

### Semantic locators (alternative to refs)

```bash
agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
agent-browser find placeholder "Search" type "query"
```

### Authentication with saved state

```bash
# Login once
agent-browser open https://app.example.com/login
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser fill @e1 "username"
agent-browser fill @e2 "password"
agent-browser click @e3
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"
agent-browser state save auth.json

# Later: load saved state
agent-browser state load auth.json
agent-browser open https://app.example.com/dashboard
```

### Cookies & Storage

```bash
agent-browser cookies                     # Get all cookies
agent-browser cookies set name value      # Set cookie
agent-browser cookies clear               # Clear cookies
agent-browser storage local               # Get localStorage
agent-browser storage local set k v       # Set value
```

### JavaScript

```bash
agent-browser eval "document.title"   # Run JavaScript
```

## Example: Form submission

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com/form
agent-browser snapshot -i
# Output shows: textbox "Email" [ref=e1], textbox "Password" [ref=e2], button "Submit" [ref=e3]

agent-browser fill @e1 "user@example.com"
agent-browser fill @e2 "password123"
agent-browser click @e3
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i  # Check result
```

## Example: Data extraction

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com/products
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser get text @e1  # Get product title
agent-browser get attr @e2 href  # Get link URL
agent-browser screenshot products.png
```

# Predator Spyware Targeting via WhatsApp: Key Findings

## Attack Method
The spyware was delivered through malicious links sent via WhatsApp messages. The attacker employed social engineering, posing as a representative of young students interested in Angola's development, using a familiar Angolan name to build trust before sending harmful links.

## Delivery Timeline
Beginning April 29, 2024, the attacker sent benign messages for several days. On May 3, 2024, the first malicious link arrived. The journalist clicked the link on May 4, resulting in successful infection. As the target later described: *"I feel naked knowing that I was the target of this invasion of my privacy."*

## Technical Details
The spyware installed itself in the directory `/private/var/containers/Bundle/` and disguised its process as "iconservicesagent," mimicking a legitimate iOS system process. The infection lasted less than a day before being removed upon device restart.

The attacker then made 11 additional reinfection attempts through July 16, 2024, all unsuccessful.

## Capabilities
According to leaked marketing materials, Predator can access encrypted messaging apps (Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram), record audio from calls and VoIP, extract emails, track GPS location, capture screenshots, activate microphones, and retrieve passwords and stored data.

# Meta/WhatsApp's Response to Spyware Threats

The article doesn't specifically mention "Predator spyware." Instead, it focuses on **NSO Group**, a spyware firm blacklisted by the US government.

## Actions Taken

**Disruption efforts:** WhatsApp successfully halted NSO-linked phishing attempts by investigating user reports and dismantling malicious accounts and groups created by the attackers.

**Legal action:** The company is seeking to hold NSO in contempt for violating a permanent injunction that previously barred them from targeting WhatsApp and its users.

**Threat intelligence:** WhatsApp shared indicators so people can "check if they were targeted by NSO-linked social engineering attempts across any platform."

**Financial support:** Meta is contributing significantly to the Spyware Accountability Initiative, which supports organizations conducting forensic research and advocacy work against spyware globally.

**User protection:** WhatsApp emphasizes that "personal messages and calls remain protected with default end-to-end encryption" and recommends users enable strict account settings and keep apps updated.

# Fake WhatsApp App Incident Summary

**What Happened:**
WhatsApp identified a malicious fake version of its iPhone app created by Italian spyware firm SIO. The company stated: "Our security team proactively identified around 200 users primarily in Italy who we believe may have downloaded this malicious unofficial client."

**Number of Users Affected:**
Approximately 200 users, predominantly located in Italy, were tricked into installing the fraudulent application.

**The Spyware:**
The malicious app was developed by SIO (an Italian government spyware maker operating through subsidiary ASIGINT). TechCrunch previously revealed that SIO distributes spyware identified as Spyrtacus, which had been embedded in various fake Android applications including counterfeit WhatsApp versions and phony customer support tools.

**Response:**
WhatsApp logged out affected users, notified them of privacy risks, and encouraged them to uninstall the fake app and download the official version. The company also announced plans to send formal legal demands to SIO to cease such activities.

### **Key Findings Summary:**

- **Delivery Method:** Predator targets WhatsApp users primarily through malicious links sent via WhatsApp messages using social engineering tactics
- **Capabilities:** The spyware can access encrypted messaging apps (WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram), record audio/VoIP calls, extract emails, track GPS location, capture screenshots, activate microphones, and retrieve passwords
- **Technical Detail:** Predator disguises itself as system processes (e.g., "iconservicesagent") on iOS devices
- **Operational Status:** Despite sanctions and public exposure, Predator remained operational through 2025, with operators continuing to adapt and source new exploits
- **Geographic Scope:** Documented attacks in Angola, Democratic Republic of Congo, Pakistan, Italy, and at least 45 countries globally
- **Meta's Response:** WhatsApp/Meta has disrupted phishing attempts, sent legal notices to spyware makers, and is pursuing legal action against NSO Group for contempt of injunctions
